acceptance: policy.host_effects in roadmap/orchestration.yaml (forbid | allow, default forbid) and an optional policy.protected_services list (name plus host:port or URL) are schema-checked; with forbid, the executor and reviewer prompts carry one block (from specy_road/host_effects.py) saying not to launch GUI apps or packaged builds, not to focus or script windows, and not to call or change the listed services or any running dev server the worker did not start; a test asserts the block in both prompts and its absence under allow

Under forbid, the tool-call guard (new tool_call_guard_host.py; tool_call_guard.py changes only its call line) denies open, xdg-open, osascript, electron and an app bundle's binary, and curl, wget or httpie requests to a protected service's host:port, each with a one-line reason naming policy.host_effects; tests per denied shape plus allowed shapes (curl to an unlisted host, open inside a quoted string argument)

The specyrd agents-team.md starter gains one commented line showing a project's host-effects rule; docs/orchestration-host-effects.md documents the policy, the denied shapes, what the guard cannot see (a test suite that itself launches an app or calls a service), and that a human acceptance run should use services the worker cannot reach

worker message <W> --interrupt stops the running turn and resumes the session with the message, on harnesses whose adapter can resume (claude-code, cursor, codex); on others it refuses and says the message will queue; the worker record logs the interrupt; a test with a fake harness asserts the turn ends and the next turn's prompt is the message. Out of scope: network sandboxing, and blocking effects inside test code

policy.protected_services entries take name, address (host:port, a URL, or a database name or DSN without credentials) and kind (http, database or port), and a roster entry may list its own protected_services, added to the project's for that worker (both schema-checked); the executor prompt's host-effects block names every entry by name and address under 'Shared services you must not touch' and says not to start a server on its port, run seeds, migrations or deletes against it, or change its data to get past an error; a test asserts each listed name and address appear in the executor prompt. Out of scope: detecting such use after the turn (post_run_check and reconcile do not see it)
nodes.title: Host effects policy: workers and reviewers do not take over the screen or change shared services, the guard denies such commands, and a message can interrupt a turn

acceptance: specy-road file-limits --write-baseline adds override_limits entries (one per bucket, named baseline-<date>-<n>) to the project's file-limits.yaml so every file failing today passes at its current worst size, bucketing files by their worst file length and worst function length rounded up (to 50 lines for files, 20 for functions); files not failing get no entry, so new files keep the default caps; --dry-run prints the entries; existing entries and comments in the YAML are kept; tests pin the buckets and that a rerun adds nothing
A failing file-limits run ends with one line naming override_limits in the config file and --write-baseline; a passing run prints no such line

upgrade's final step runs file-limits and prints the failure count before and after the version change when it can tell them apart (the stamped version's measurement is not available, so it prints the count and, when it is not zero, says that measurement rules may have changed and points at --write-baseline); it never fails upgrade on file-limits. Out of scope: files that upgrade's own writes push over the cap (M13.2), and the CHANGELOG line (release notes are human-owned)
nodes.title: file-limits can write a baseline of today's exceptions, a failing run points at it, and upgrade reports the file-limits count

acceptance: chore start <slug> --worktree creates the branch (chore/<slug>) and the worktree when they do not exist, from the integration branch's tip, and runs env_setup there as pickup --worktree does (worktree_env.setup_worktree_env); a test asserts branch, worktree and the env_setup marker
chore zones <slug> --add <path> (repeatable) widens a chore's touch zones and records who and when; worker reconcile then accepts files under the added zone; a test covers reconcile before and after

review-packet, prompt --role reviewer and review record accept a chore slug wherever they accept a node id (resolved through review_target, the chore's base..head), and chore close records 'reviewed' with the verdict when a review exists for the chore's head; tests for each command

The managed .gitignore block lists work/chores/ (records stay local unless a project opts in by deleting the line); upgrade adds it to existing repos through the managed block. Out of scope: chore records in the digest
nodes.title: Chores at parity with leaves: worktree, branch and env_setup on start, widen zones, the review-record path, and work/chores ignored

acceptance: An acceptance item starting 'observed(<role>[, <tier>]):' (schema description and docs) can only be satisfied by a recorded observation on the planning sheet ('A#: observed by <name> as <role> on <tier>, <date>: <result>'), as human: items need a decision; finish-this-task refuses while one lacks it; reviewers mark it n/a with reason 'observed', and an executor's READY or summary cannot satisfy it

review-packet (through review_packet_observed.py; review_packet.py is at its 400-line cap) flags executor text (summary or READY) that claims a role, stage, server or walkthrough observation for an observed( item, quoting the line and saying it is executor-supplied; a test with the reported shape (timings measured inside pytest presented as a role-observed table) asserts the flag

The reviewer prompt separates coordinator-supplied probes (a 'Coordinator probes' section: run them and report; a failure is a finding, not an acceptance failure unless an acceptance item covers it) from acceptance items; a test asserts the section heading and wording. Out of scope: verifying who made an observation
nodes.title: Role-observed acceptance needs evidence from that role, and coordinator probes are not acceptance
